summary: This note is a Wikipedia-sourced description of Crooked Run, a stream that is a tributary of Catawissa Creek in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania. It flows through North Union Township and is classed as a High-Quality Coldwater Fishery and Class A Wild Trout Waters, yet it is impaired by atmospheric deposition. The note also lists the main rock formations and soils in the stream's watershed. The length and watershed area values are blank in the note.
one_line: Crooked Run is a Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania tributary of Catawissa Creek, noted for its coldwater trout fishery and atmospheric deposition impairment.
key_facts: Crooked Run is a tributary of Catawissa Creek in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, in the United States.
Crooked Run flows through North Union Township.
Crooked Run is considered a High-Quality Coldwater Fishery.
Crooked Run is considered Class A Wild Trout Waters.
Crooked Run is impaired by atmospheric deposition.
The main rock formations in the Crooked Run watershed are the Mauch Chunk Formation and the Pocono Formation.
The main soils in the Crooked Run watershed are the Leck Kill soil and the Hazleton soil.
The note gives the length of Crooked Run as approximately a value that is missing from the text.
The note gives the watershed area of Crooked Run, but the numeric value is missing from the text.
The source of the note is Wikipedia.
